chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'How is the greeting to the inhabitants of the graves?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, you should say: Peace be upon the people of the dwellings, from the Muslims and the Believers. You have preceded us, and we, God willing, will be joining you.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الدِّيَارِ: People of the dwellings (referring to graves)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct Islamic greeting to say when visiting the graves?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the canonical formula for saluting the dead, rooted in the Quranic verse of the People of the Cave (Surah Al-Kahf 18:25), which underscores the spiritual continuity between the living and the deceased. It reflects the Shia practice of maintaining a tangible connection with the faithful who have preceded us, affirming that death is not a severance but a transition within the same community of believers.
